services.title: Long-Term Care and Medicaid Planning
services.summary: Paying for nursing home, assisted living or home care.
services.text: Personal care is expensive, whether at home, in assisted living or in a nursing home. We help seniors and their families protect savings and receive the benefits and care to which they are entitled.
services.lead: In Texas, nursing homes can cost as much as $70,000.00 a year, and providing the same level of care at home or in assisted living can be even more expensive. These costs, for the most part, are not covered by Medicare. Texas Medicaid pays for nursing home care for those who qualify and, in some instances, for assisted living and home care.

covers.title: Advance planning
covers.text: Planning with clients in good health, or who have just been diagnosed with an illness, before care is needed.

covers.title: Planning in a crisis
covers.text: Working with the families of seniors who are already hospitalized or in a nursing home. It is never too late to plan.

covers.title: The Medicaid application
covers.text: The rules are complicated and ever-changing, and the application process can be daunting. Our firm has guided seniors and their families through it for more than thirty years.

covers.title: Protecting the healthy spouse
covers.text: Paying for long-term care out of savings can leave a healthy spouse destitute and deplete the inheritance a family worked long and hard to leave.

questions.q: My parents are aging. How can I help them to remain independent and protect their assets?
questions.a: Few of today's seniors carry long-term care insurance, so they must rely on savings to cover the cost of care. We plan ahead where we can, and apply for the benefits they qualify for where care is already needed.

questions.q: Does Medicare pay for long-term care?
questions.a: For the most part, no. These costs are covered by long-term care insurance, and by Texas Medicaid for those who qualify.

services.title: Special Needs Planning
services.summary: Planning for a child or adult with a disability.
services.text: We work with parents of children with special needs to ensure that the care and support they provide will be carried forward after the parents are gone.
services.lead: Parents of children with special needs often face years of expensive care for their children that may be exhausting and overwhelming. One of the most important things they can do today is to create an estate plan for tomorrow.

covers.title: Trusts that preserve benefits
covers.text: Our attorneys establish special needs and supplemental needs trusts to manage assets and preserve public benefits.

covers.title: Federal and state programs
covers.text: We help guide families through the intricate maze of federal and state programs for disabled family members.

covers.title: Guardians and trustees
covers.text: The planning process includes naming guardians, creating trusts and choosing trustees.

covers.title: Care and housing
covers.text: Finding care providers and arranging housing as necessary, with each plan tailored to the needs of the children and the wishes of their parents.

questions.q: My child has a disability. How can I protect and plan for her future?
questions.a: Each plan must be tailored to meet the needs of the children and the wishes of their parents. We use trusts, named guardians, chosen trustees, care providers and housing arrangements as the family's situation calls for them.

services.imageAlt: An adult and a child walking hand in hand through a park

services.title: Special Needs Trusts
services.summary: Trusts that hold assets without losing benefits.
services.text: Our attorneys are experts in establishing special needs and supplemental needs trusts to manage assets and preserve public benefits.
services.lead: A special needs or supplemental needs trust holds assets for a person with a disability without costing them the public benefits they rely on. Pi-Yi Mayo has built a national reputation as an expert in elder law and special needs trusts, and the firm has established more than six hundred of them.

questions.q: Can a trust hold a settlement or inheritance without ending benefits?
questions.a: That is what these trusts are for: they manage assets while preserving eligibility for public benefits. We establish first-party and third-party trusts and advise on distributions from them.

services.title: Estate Planning
services.summary: Wills, powers of attorney and deeds.
services.text: Wills, powers of attorney, partition agreements and deeds, drawn up with long-term care and public benefits in mind rather than apart from them.
services.lead: Both partners practise estate planning, and Bryn Poland often speaks about it to civic organizations, churches and support groups for children with disabilities. The firm publishes the worksheets it uses for a new will, powers of attorney, a partition agreement and a deed, so clients can gather what is needed before the first meeting.

covers.title: Wills
covers.text: Drafted from the firm's new will worksheet.

covers.title: Powers of attorney
covers.text: Financial and medical powers of attorney, with the firm's own worksheet to work from.

covers.title: Deeds and partition agreements
covers.text: Deed and partition agreement worksheets for property held by a couple or a family.

covers.title: Planning alongside benefits
covers.text: An estate plan written so it does not disturb Medicaid eligibility or a disabled beneficiary's public benefits.

services.title: Probate
services.summary: Administering an estate through the court.
services.text: Probate of an estate in the Texas courts, including establishing a decedent's estate in probate court in order to pursue litigation.
services.lead: Probate is a practice area of both partners, and the firm publishes a legal guide to it. Where a claim survives the person who held it, the firm also establishes a decedent's estate in probate court so that litigation can be pursued.

services.title: Guardianship
services.text: Guardianships and conservatorships for adults and children who cannot manage their own affairs, including guardian ad litem services.
services.lead: Guardianship is a practice area of both partners, and the firm publishes a legal guide to it. The firm acts in guardianships and conservatorships and provides guardian ad litem services to the court.

services.title: Trust Administration
services.summary: Running a trust after it is established.
services.text: Administration of special needs and supplemental needs trusts after they are established, including counselling trustees on distributions.

services.title: Veteran's Aid & Attendance
services.summary: VA pension benefits for veterans needing care.
services.text: Aid and attendance pension benefits for veterans and surviving spouses, and how those benefits interact with Medicaid eligibility. Pi-Yi Mayo holds V.A. Accreditation from the Department of Veterans Affairs.

services.title: Medicare
services.text: Medicare coverage questions, appeals, conditional payments, liens and set-aside arrangements. The firm has published papers on each of these.

services.title: Personal Injury Settlement Planning
services.summary: Protecting a settlement and the benefits with it.
services.text: A comprehensive array of legal services for injured people, their families and their trial attorneys, in settling claims and managing settlement funds.
services.lead: We focus on preserving settlement proceeds for a plaintiff's lifetime needs and ensuring the settlement will enhance the individual's life in a manner that maintains eligibility for public benefits, if appropriate. Our work complements that of trial attorneys and allows them to focus on maximizing the settlement while reducing malpractice exposure.

covers.title: Advice for trial attorneys
covers.text: We advise attorneys on Medicare conditional payments and set aside arrangements, Medicaid claims, Special Needs Trusts, and Qualified Settlement Funds.

covers.title: Establishing and funding trusts
covers.text: The court process to establish and fund trusts with personal injury proceeds, and the preservation of public benefits.

covers.title: Liens and set-asides
covers.text: Medicare set-aside arrangements and coordination with lien resolution advisors.

covers.title: Managing the money
covers.text: Fund management, identifying appropriate trustees, counselling on settlement structures and tax reduction.

covers.title: Court appointments
covers.text: Guardianships and conservatorships, guardian ad litem services, and establishing a decedent's estate in probate court in order to pursue litigation.

questions.q: I just settled my lawsuit. How do I keep my public benefits? Should I structure the proceeds? Do I have to pay off any liens?
questions.a: We work with individuals, their families, and their trusted financial advisors to create a plan for managing recovered funds, identifying appropriate trustees, and preserving vital public benefits. Our goal is to help the clients protect their settlements while providing for greater quality of life.

services.title: Qualified Settlement Funds
services.text: Pi-Yi Mayo serves as administrator to more than 70 qualified settlement funds from jurisdictions all over the United States, with nearly $80,000,000.00 under management.
services.lead: A qualified settlement fund holds settlement proceeds while liens are resolved, trusts are established and allocations are worked out. Pi-Yi Mayo serves as administrator to more than 70 of them from jurisdictions all over the United States, and Bryn Poland speaks on the subject at continuing education conferences for attorneys and trust officers.

about.title: The firm's practice is dedicated to senior citizens, people with disabilities, their families and advocates.
text: We can provide expertise on any issue facing senior citizens: from long-term care and estate planning issues, to public benefits and health-care coverage. Pi-Yi Mayo has served the state of Texas as an attorney for over 30 years and has worked to build a national reputation as an attorney dedicated to meeting the needs of people with disabilities.

Bryn Poland joined the firm of Pi-Yi Mayo in 2007 and partnered with Pi-Yi in 2018 to form Mayo & Poland, PLLC. We work hard to partner with advocates for people with disabilities to provide assistance with subrogation claims, Medicare Set-Asides, Special Needs Trusts, and Qualified Settlement Funds.

Hiring an elder law attorney usually comes in the midst of a family crisis. We understand that reaching out for legal advice can add to an already stressful situation. Mayo & Poland strive to provide practical and helpful legal advice with a personal touch. We serve our clients and their families best by taking the time to understand family dynamics - not just legal facts.

values.title: A personal touch
values.text: Clients can expect prompt and professional service with a big side of Texas hospitality.

values.title: Experience that sees ahead
values.text: Even after the primary legal issues have been settled, new and often unforeseen issues arise. Because of our experience we can identify and solve them before they cause additional stress.

values.title: Proactive communication
values.text: We strive to maintain proactive communication with clients and pride ourselves on our ability to get results as quickly as possible.

team.name: Pi-Yi Mayo
team.bio: A lifelong Baytown resident, Pi-Yi earned both his undergraduate and law degrees at the University of Houston. In a career spanning over 30 years he has extensive experience in elder law, Medicaid planning, special needs trusts, disability law and veteran's benefits. He is a Certified Elder Law Attorney by the National Elder Law Foundation, holds V.A. Accreditation, is a past president of the Texas Chapter of NAELA and a founding member and past president (2012) of the Special Needs Alliance. He has authored more than 50 papers and presented hundreds of speeches to attorneys, CPAs, government entities, judges and families. Away from the office he is an avid outdoorsman who enjoys hunting and fishing, and takes his greatest joy in time with his family and grandchildren.

team.name: Bryn Poland
team.bio: Born and raised in Kansas, Bryn earned her undergraduate degree from Kansas State University and her law degree from Washburn University School of Law, where she was a staff member and two-time published writer of the Washburn Law Journal. She was inspired to become an elder law attorney watching her family struggle with care options for her great grandmother, Lulu Sleeper, who lived to the age of 109. Licensed to practice in Texas and Kansas, she focuses on estate planning, special needs trust planning and administration, Medicaid planning and qualified settlement funds. She is a member and past president of the Elder Law Committee of the Houston Bar Association, sits on the Continuing Legal Education Committee of the Houston Bar Association, serves on the Houston Midtown Management District Board of Directors, is an active member of the Houston Area Kansas State University Alumni Club, and speaks frequently at continuing education conferences for attorneys and trust officers.

faqs.q: What is this going to cost me?
faqs.a: We invite the question, because we want to be up-front about our fees to ensure the engagement of our firm is the best fit for our clients. Every case is different, but whenever possible we use a flat fee for our legal services rather than billing by the hour.

faqs.q: How is each fee worked out?
faqs.a: Each fee is determined based on the complexity of the case, an estimate of the amount of time the matter will take, and the anticipated value we plan to add to the client matter. Though we generally find our fees are within industry standards for our areas of practice, we won't compete with other attorneys on price.

faqs.q: Why a flat fee rather than hourly billing?
faqs.a: Our clients appreciate fixed fees rather than the uncertainty that comes with hourly billing. Flat fees help clients understand exactly what our services cost, and we find it encourages communication because clients can call with any question without worrying they will be billed for additional time.

faqs.q: Is it ever too late to plan?
faqs.a: It is never too late to plan. We work both with clients in good health or newly diagnosed, and with families of seniors who are already hospitalized or in a nursing home.

faqs.q: Do you work with other attorneys?
faqs.a: Yes. Our work complements that of trial attorneys and allows them to focus on maximizing the settlement while reducing malpractice exposure. We advise them on Medicare conditional payments and set aside arrangements, Medicaid claims, Special Needs Trusts and Qualified Settlement Funds.

faqs.q: Will Bryn speak to our group?
faqs.a: Bryn often speaks about estate planning and special needs trusts to civic organizations, churches and support groups for children with disabilities. Call the office to ask about a date.
